question: Can the 1990 Calancan Bay fish survey support a reliable historical bay-level species baseline?

source.title: Effects of Mine Tailings on the Fishery Resources of Calancan Bay
source.license: The current NFRDI page footer states site contents are CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise stated; the scanned 1990 article has no separate license statement in its printed pages reviewed.
source.access: Official NFRDI article page and full nine-page scanned PDF were reviewed. The PDF was inspected locally for this review and was not copied into the repository.

studyScope.habitat: Marine coral-reef and coastal bay waters
studyScope.fishSurveyDates: The article does not clearly state that every fish observation and compiled landing/interview record shares the hydrobiological sampling dates.
studyScope.stationCoverage: The article describes eight stations for fish, benthic and seawater sample collection and nine underwater survey stations; the figure numbers stations but gives no coordinate table or taxon-by-station crosswalk.
studyScope.notCovered: No freshwater river, lake, reservoir or inland wetland coverage is established by this marine bay study.

integrityFindings.resultsVisualSurveyCount: 85 fish species representing 21 families recorded by visual counting
integrityFindings.table4EntryCountNote: Manual count of the printed Table 4 labels across its family headings; entries include genus-only, spp. and unidentified/family-level placeholders and therefore are not 72 resolved species.
integrityFindings.countConflict: The article does not reconcile the abstract/discussion total of 108, the results statement of 85 visual-survey species, and the 72 manually counted displayed Table 4 labels. Survey methods also combine visual observations, fish landings and interviews in the compiled index.
taxonomicCaveats: Table 4 uses abbreviated genus names, spp. labels and unidentified group-level entries; these need source-string transcription and current specialist-taxonomy review before normalization.
A few labels appear under family headings that do not obviously match the listed genus; retain source placement verbatim until independently checked.
integrityFindings.disposition: Historical Calancan Bay fishery evidence only. Keep the numerical totals and list held; do not publish a normalized checklist or infer current presence from this review.

limits: The report is a historical, pollution-era marine fishery/reef study, not a current inventory and not freshwater coverage.
No coordinate table or species-by-station association is supplied, so the fish list cannot be placed at the numbered reef/hydrobiology stations.
The 85, 108 and manually counted table-label totals are not reconciled; genus-only and family-level labels prevent treating all table entries as species.
The article describes the compiled fish index as drawing on observations, interviews, stations and landings; it is not a single uniform sample frame.
No current abundance, catchability, natural diet, legal access, fishing rules, water quality or safety status follows from this 1981-era evidence.

The NFRDI website currently states CC BY 4.0 for site contents unless otherwise stated, while the older article's printed pages do not carry a separate license statement; retain attribution and review item scope before any later table transformation.

followUp.nextAction: Search for a more recent, locality-resolved Calancan Bay assessment and an independent open coastal fish inventory for Santa Cruz. Preserve this 1990 paper as a separate historic survey and do not treat its pollution-era observations as current conditions.
